whatItDoes: line-drift.mjs (Node built-ins + git, read-only) extracts every path:line citation (including bare :N continuations and plain-text ones), backticked repo path and 7-12/40-hex commit from 26 Aster control-plane documents and judges each against the checkout: OK, PARTIAL, MOVED (with where the paired snippet is now), GONE, IN-RANGE, PAST-EOF, MISSING-PATH, IGNORED (git check-ignore, INV-034), UNTRACKED, UNREACHABLE-COMMIT (full clones only), NOT-A-COMMIT or UNCHECKABLE with a reason; every drift finding is re-judged at the commit its text first appeared (git log -S), the commit that last edited its line (git blame) and a commit its sentence/paragraph names, with context hints, an allowlist and --accept-annotated. At 62ddb17 it reads 1,316 references and flags 96 drift + 2 PARTIAL; I hand-adjudicated all 98 in adjudication.json (30 need a fix, 63 true-but-expected, 5 false alarms), and index.html presents the run with filters, a per-document chart and a Try-it panel running the same pure module on pasted text.

deviationsFromProposal: Verified every citation; corrected: (a) the proposal expected main.ts:637 'Grid spans' MOVED to :647 - it is GONE because 446e3a7 replaced the literal with a derived label; the test pins GONE and the stale STATUS item is the finding. (b) Both proposed MISSING-PATH examples (src/v2/launch-vehicles.ts, tier-sizing-results.json) are already annotated in their own founding docs (SLICE_15:212, SLICE_18:245); the tool reports them with 'annotated at' context and --accept-annotated excuses them. (c) .githooks/pre-commit:53 is indeed a comment, but because f7b19e7 fixed the bug; reported as GONE with C17 stale. (d) mcp/README cites compute-shared.ts relative to mcp/, so resolution tries the document folder. (e) The proposal's hand counts (16 STATUS citations, 32 across INVARIANTS + Slice 15-19) differ from the tool's (35 and 38) because the tool counts bare :N and plain-text citations. (f) The 300-byte STATUS:417-419 snapshot became a 1,073-byte 417-425 excerpt plus three more excerpts and three whole target files (.gitignore, pre-commit, porkchop main.ts) so offline tests can judge real targets. Added beyond the proposal: PARTIAL status (misquote is not drift), first-appeared (git log -S) and last-edited (git blame) history alongside the named-commit check, paragraph-level pinning, context hints (says-gone, annotated, plan, foreign), force-added detection (INV-034's other half), placeholder names, a 7-12-or-40 commit rule with hash context (the first full-history run's 10 UNREACHABLE-COMMIT were all hashes), a full hand adjudication of all 98 findings in adjudication.json, a full-history clone run (example-full-history.txt) made in scratch and deleted, and a browser page. Pairing heuristics (80-char gap, connective words, clause-break penalty) were tuned on this corpus, which the README states.
notBuilt: Not proven: the snippet-pairing and context heuristics were tuned on Aster's own documents and have not been measured on another corpus; the 98-finding adjudication is one reader's (no second adjudication); 53 IN-RANGE citations have no snippet so stale line numbers there are invisible; 'first appeared' (git log -S) can predate a later repeated occurrence of the same reference. The full-history numbers (577 commits resolve, history column) come from a clone made in scratch and deleted; the test that re-derives them runs only with LINE_DRIFT_FULL_CLONE set (I ran it: 26/26 pass). The tool cannot distinguish shorthand names (view.ts for porkchop-view.ts), files in other repositories, or most placeholders from genuinely missing paths. Not wired into Aster session start or CI, and no allowlist for Aster was committed (proposed in README only). Not through Aster's multi-agent audit, founding-doc DEC process for the vocabulary, or protected-path dispatch for AGENTS.md.
